issues.description: Method 'dd_get_amplitude' has conflicting return-type/specification across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md, lines 48-51) instructs students to implement dd_get_amplitude to "return the probability corresponding to the given bitstring as a float." In the template implementation (template_repository/dd_simulation.py, line 355) and in the reference solution (solution_repository/dd_simulation.py, line 381) the function is declared to return an np.complex128 and its docstring and implementation compute and return the complex amplitude for the given bitstring. This mismatch (probability float vs. complex amplitude) will confuse students and likely cause incorrect submissions or failing tests if a student follows the problem statement instead of the template/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the implementations. Preferred fix: update the problem statement to request that dd_get_amplitude return the complex amplitude (np.complex128) and clarify the difference between amplitude and measurement probability (and where to square/abs to get probability). Alternative: change template and solution to provide a dd_get_probability (returning a float) and rename the task accordingly; update tests to call the renamed function. Prefer the first option because both template and solution already implement and use the complex amplitude.
